methods.core_law: For f=P delta_q - nu after cancellation, every table has norm abs(P-N+a_I)+a_I and sum_I a_I >= 10N. methods.name: BRC error linearization / Pell-Pade tail transport
capabilities: exact recursive BRC gap orbit with second difference -2 and third difference 0
exact integer Pell-Pade lower approximant to sqrt((m+h)/m) for h=1,2
second-order linear recurrence in Pade order X_(n+2)=(4m+2h)X_(n+1)-h^2 X_n
exact integer <=2-correction certificate J h^(2n+1)<=m A_n B_n
methods.core_law: For E_K=sqrt(1+x)-1-P_K, derivatives above order K satisfy (1+x)E_K^(n+1)/E_K^n=1/2-n, while ordinary BRC correction gaps satisfy G_q=G_0-q(2a+q). The diagonal Pade/Pell approximant obtained from (1+sqrt(1+x))^(2n+1)=P_n+sqrt(1+x)Q_n yields homogenized integers A_n,B_n with (m+h)B_n^2-mA_n^2=h^(2n+1). This makes A_n/B_n a rigorous lower sqrt-ratio predictor and gives the exact sufficient certificate J h^(2n+1)<=m A_n B_n for at most two BRC basin corrections.
methods.hard_boundary: Classical Pade/Pell approximation is prior art. The current contribution is exact BRC composition, certification, and error-linearization bookkeeping. The Python reference path is substantially faster than the previous high-order Taylor table-free tail but still slower than direct optimized isqrt on isolated steps. No asymptotic factorization speedup, RSA-practicality, optimal multiplier order, or Foundation promotion is claimed.

methods.name: BRC order-one linear deep-tail multiplier transport
capabilities: exact order-one Pell lower ratio (4m+3h)/(4m+h) for h=1,2
root increment predictor floor(2hJ/(4m+h)) without sqrt-ratio tables
exact state-dependent two-correction certificate J h^3 <= m(4m+3h)(4m+h)
single common odd-N mod-8 tail threshold 4m^5 >= N
unbounded multiplier stream beyond the previous max_multiplier<=100 table boundary
finite full-pipeline speedup over fair incremental direct-isqrt baselines in tested 512..8192-bit cohorts
methods.core_law: For h in {1,2}, the order-one Pell pair A=4m+3h, B=4m+h satisfies (m+h)B^2-mA^2=h^3 and A/B<sqrt((m+h)/m). Therefore d=floor(2hJ/(4m+h)) is a lower root increment. If J h^3<=mAB, at most two BRC odd-width corrections recover the exact target root/remainder. Since J<=sqrt(mN) and A,B>=4m, the root-free condition 256m^5>=N h^6 suffices; h=2 yields the common mod-8 tail condition 4m^5>=N.
methods.hard_boundary: This is an exact multiplier-state transport optimization only. It does not reduce a Lehman/Hart-style N^(1/3) factor-search horizon, prove an asymptotic factorization speedup, or imply RSA practicality. The deep-tail threshold is enormous at RSA bit sizes. Finite Python speedups are implementation evidence, not machine-model complexity theorems.
